variants.context: Continual learning is the ability of a machine-learning system to learn from a stream of new tasks or data while retaining useful knowledge from earlier tasks. It matters when the world changes after deployment: the system must adapt without catastrophic forgetting, uncontrolled regressions, or a full retraining cycle for every new pattern.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “What is Continual Learning?”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.detail: Separate persistent drift or a new task from noise, seasonality, and instrumentation failures.

pairs.label: Build the update set
pairs.detail: Combine recent examples with a bounded replay sample or another preservation mechanism.
pairs.explanation: Combine recent examples with a bounded replay sample or another preservation mechanism.

pairs.label: Adapt under constraints
pairs.detail: Update selected parameters while regularization, memory, or modular structure protects prior knowledge.

pairs.label: Test transfer and forgetting

variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Separate the three learning scenarios”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Task-incremental
pairs.detail: The system learns a sequence of distinct tasks and can route each request to the appropriate task head.
pairs.explanation: The system learns a sequence of distinct tasks and can route each request to the appropriate task head. For example, one model family may add detection after classification.

pairs.label: Domain-incremental
pairs.detail: The task and labels stay the same, but the input domain moves.
pairs.explanation: The task and labels stay the same, but the input domain moves. A sentiment model may adapt from electronics reviews to grocery reviews without receiving a domain label at inference time.

pairs.label: Class-incremental
pairs.detail: New classes arrive while the model must still recognize old classes.
pairs.explanation: New classes arrive while the model must still recognize old classes. This is difficult because the model cannot assume which class group a request belongs to.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. Use the full lesson’s worked examples and interactive labs to explore the trade-offs behind these questions.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Task-incremental: The system learns a sequence of distinct tasks and can route each request to the appropriate task head. Domain-incremental: The task and labels stay the same, but the input domain moves. Class-incremental: New classes arrive while the model must still recognize old classes.

variants.prompt: What does the stability-plasticity trade-off describe?

Balancing CPU usage with disk capacity
variants.explanation: Plasticity enables adaptation to new data, while stability prevents the update from erasing useful prior behavior.
